summary: Demo tenant: imported "Standard Demo - Latency/Cost/Errors" dashboard missing panels and showing empty queries after import
description:
Issue summary
- Sales/SEs are importing the prebuilt dashboard export for the demo tenant, but several panels do not appear after import (or appear with "No data" / empty query editor).
- This is impacting the Standard Demo v1 runthrough, specifically the sections that rely on showing token cost breakdown and error analysis.

Impact
- Demo reliability risk: during live demos, SEs lose the "single pane of glass" story and have to explain missing panels.
- Increased pre-demo prep time: folks are rebuilding panels manually.

Who reported / where
- Reported by: Markus Klein (Solutions Engineering)
- First seen in: Demo tenant Console > Dashboards (imported from observability-pack export)
- Slack context: #sales and #eng-platform threads about dashboard import stability

Steps to reproduce
1) In the demo tenant Console, go to Observability → Dashboards.
2) Click Import dashboard.
3) Upload the exported dashboard JSON ("redwood-demo-standard-v1" export from Observability Pack).
4) Leave defaults (folder + datasource mapping) and click Import.
5) Observe: dashboard loads, but 4–7 panels are missing OR present but show blank query definitions.

Expected
- All panels present (Latency p50/p95, Token cost per request, Cache hit ratio, 4xx/5xx breakdown, Throttles/429 rate) with working queries.

Actual
- Panels referencing templated variables (e.g., $tenant_id, $route, $model) and/or specific datasource UID fail to import cleanly.
- Some panels import but lose query JSON (query editor opens with empty state).

Notes / initial hypotheses
- Likely mismatch between exported datasource UID/name and the demo tenant datasource UID.
- Dashboard export was generated from staging; demo tenant is prod (different datasource IDs).
- Some panels depend on dashboard variables that are not being created on import (variable block may be stripped/blocked by Console validation).

Requested outcome
- Identify root cause and publish updated import instructions for the demo tenant.
- If needed, update the exported dashboard artifact to be demo-tenant-safe (no hard-coded datasource UID; ensure variables are included).
comments: 2025-01-14 09:18 Markus Klein: Hitting this consistently when prepping for tomorrow’s enterprise platform demo. Import succeeds but the Token Cost and Error panels are missing/blank. We can’t have people rebuilding panels manually. Can someone from Console/Obs take point? I can share the JSON export we’re using if needed.

2025-01-14 10:02 Chloe Martin (assignee): Taking. Can you confirm which export version you used (date/hash) and whether you mapped datasource during import? Also: does the Console import flow show any warnings in the UI banner?

2025-01-14 10:21 Markus Klein: Using the export from Observability Pack PR (latest in the enablement folder). No warnings shown. We left datasource mapping as default (it just shows one option and we click through). After import, panels like "Token Cost / Request" and "5xx by Route" are missing; variables dropdown is also empty.

2025-01-14 12:37 Logan Wright: I pulled logs from the dashboard-import service for demo tenant. We are sanitizing dashboard JSON on import and currently drop templating.variables entries when they include "datasource": {"uid": ...} blocks we don’t recognize. That causes downstream panels that reference $tenant_id/$route to render with empty queries. This was added as a safety check for cross-tenant imports but it’s too strict for our own prebuilt exports.

2025-01-14 13:05 Chloe Martin: Reproduced. Root cause seems to be a combination of (1) hard-coded datasource UID in the exported panels and templating variables and (2) our import sanitizer removing the variable definitions when UID mismatch occurs. Result: panels that rely on variables load without query context and appear blank/missing.

Immediate workaround for field: during import, use "Advanced" and explicitly map the datasource to "redwood-metrics" (demo tenant) AND toggle "Keep templating variables" (hidden under advanced). This is not obvious and is why people are clicking through and getting broken dashboards.

2025-01-15 09:44 Chloe Martin: I’ve drafted updated import instructions for the demo tenant runbook (step-by-step + screenshots needed). Also proposing we re-export a demo-tenant-safe dashboard artifact that uses datasource name instead of UID. Logan: can your team generate a new export without UIDs (or with __inputs)?

2025-01-15 11:12 Logan Wright: Yes. We can publish a new dashboard export that uses __inputs and datasource placeholders (Grafana-style), so import prompts the user to map datasource. Also recommend we rename variables to be stable ($tenant, $route, $model) and include defaults for demo tenant. I’ll coordinate with Observability Pack repo.

2025-01-16 16:28 Chloe Martin: Updated artifact is ready internally and confirmed import works end-to-end in demo tenant. Panels present and queries intact. Also verified the cost panels render once there’s recent traffic (ran demo scripts to generate sample requests). Publishing updated instructions + linking the new artifact location.
2025-01-17 10:06 Markus Klein: Confirmed fixed using the new export + the updated import steps. All panels show up. This unblocks Standard Demo v1 dry run.
root_cause: Dashboard JSON export contained hard-coded datasource UIDs and variable definitions tied to the source environment. The demo tenant import flow sanitizes/validates dashboard JSON and dropped templating variable blocks when datasource UID did not match, which caused dependent panels to render with missing/blank query definitions.
resolution: Published a demo-tenant-safe dashboard export that uses datasource inputs/placeholders (no environment-specific UIDs) and includes stable templating variables with defaults. Updated demo tenant import instructions to require explicit datasource mapping via Advanced import options. Verified successful import and panel rendering after generating sample traffic in the demo tenant.
workaround: Use Observability → Dashboards → Import → Advanced, explicitly map datasource to the demo tenant metrics datasource ("redwood-metrics"), and ensure "Keep templating variables" is enabled before completing import.
follow_ups: 1) Product: adjust dashboard import sanitizer to preserve templating variables when datasource UID mismatches but a valid datasource mapping is provided. 2) Enablement: refresh screenshot guide for the deck/runbook so SEs can validate dashboards quickly pre-demo. 3) Add a pre-demo check step: run demo scenario script to generate recent traffic so panels don’t appear empty.
